correctness.rationale: A/J^2 generation lifts by nilpotence: J=(B∩J)+J² and powers J^s⊆(B∩J)^s+J^{s+1}. Semisimple vertex labels must be distinct. Conjugacy of square-zero complements removes exactly the difference-label direction from every nonloop bimodule component, and none from loop components; remaining uniform matrices give independent full-rank factors. The birthday log expansion and an O(v q^{M-r}) arrow union bound prove the limiting law. Thirteen complete prime-field test cases pass, including two algebras with identical first radical layer but different higher products.

value.rationale: The probability that a random tuple generates a finite algebra is an intrinsic quantitative invariant; here it is computed in closed form for all dimensions and all higher relations in an infinite family. The exact threshold determines minimal generators, and the nonloop one-direction loss exposes the structural difference between bimodule arrows and loops. The sparse birthday limit reveals a universal phase transition independent of quiver orientation, higher algebra relations, and bounded edge multiplicities.
